growth_stages.name: Nursery
growth_stages.description: Seedlings raised on clean beds from disease-free seed for 30-45 days before transplanting. Day 0 is transplanting, not seed sowing -- same convention as tomato.json.

growth_stages.name: Harvesting
growth_stages.description: Repeated weekly/bi-weekly picking over months. The source ruleset gives this stage as '61-150+ DAT', i.e. open-ended -- 150 is used here as this crop file's typical_duration_days, not a stated ceiling.

operations.name: Land Clearing
operations.description: Removal of vegetation/debris from the plot.

operations.name: Land Preparation
operations.description: Ploughing/bed formation. NOTE: the source ruleset's Stage 1 also names a rotation check here ('avoid planting immediately after tomato -- they share bacterial wilt and viruses; system flags this from plot history') that this knowledge base's engine cannot currently implement -- see version_history for why, flagged for the end-of-round engine review.

operations.name: Nursery Establishment
operations.description: Sowing seed in nursery beds on clean, disease-free ground.

operations.name: Transplanting
operations.description: Moving seedlings from nursery to the field at ~60cm x 50cm spacing, with basal manure + NPK. This is day 0 of the field lifecycle.

operations.name: Split Fertilizer Application
operations.description: Fertilizer applied in split doses across the season to sustain the crop through its long fruiting window -- unlike a single-harvest cereal, one basal dose is not enough to carry a plant that keeps fruiting for months.

operations.name: Pest & Disease Scouting/Control
operations.description: Pepper Veinal Mottle Virus (PVMV), mites, and fruit fly monitoring/vector control.

operations.name: Harvest (Picking)
operations.description: Picking ripe fruit. Like tomato, this REPEATS many times across months as successive fruit ripen -- there is no single terminal harvest event. The source ruleset also specifies a rotation-check ('avoid planting immediately after tomato') referenced on the land_preparation operation -- that rule is STILL not implemented, since it requires checking a different crop's plot history, a Group C item beyond this engine-fixes pass's scope. The harvest-frequency data-integrity check ('more than 3 times in 7 days is blocked, flag if >2/week'), which was ALSO previously unimplemented, is now implemented -- see pepper_r_harvest_frequency_block/warn in validation_rules.

operations.name: Post-Harvest Handling
operations.description: Moving picked ripe fruit quickly to market, or promptly drying chili-type pods.

validation_rules.condition: Land preparation cannot be logged before land clearing. Interval not independently stated for pepper in the source ruleset -- carried over as the default used across this knowledge base's other crop files, same pattern as tomato_r1. Flagged for review.
validation_rules.source: General cross-crop default (same pattern as tomato.json, maize.json).

validation_rules.condition: Nursery is normally started around the time land clearing/preparation begins, since it runs for several weeks while the main field is prepared in parallel. Same unsourced-default pattern as tomato_r2. Flagged for review.
validation_rules.source: General cross-reference with tomato.json's analogous rule -- not independently sourced for pepper timing specifically.

validation_rules.condition: Land preparation must be logged at least 1 day before transplanting, and no more than 21 days before it.
validation_rules.internal_note: PLATFORM BUGFIX: this dependency rule did not exist at all in the original file, meaning transplanting could previously be logged with NO land_preparation in history whatsoever (not even same-day -- any day, or never). Added in response to a real bug the user found: land preparation needs to happen and be given at least a day before the next stage begins, not be skippable or same-day. min=1 day (not 0) so same-day submissions are also blocked, consistent with the same fix applied to every other crop file in this pass.
validation_rules.source: N/A -- internal platform bugfix, not new agronomic sourcing. Max-day window (21 days) matches the convention used for equivalent rules in this knowledge base's other annual/nursery-transplant crops.

validation_rules.condition: The source ruleset states the nursery duration as '30-45 days on clean beds' descriptively, without the explicit separate hard-block/soft-warning wording it gives tomato's nursery rule (tomato_r3/tomato_r3b in tomato.json, which has an explicit 15-45 day hard block plus a narrower 21-35 day warning band). No hard block is invented here that the source doesn't itself state for this crop -- implemented as a single warning band matching the source's stated 30-45 day range.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Recommended Varieties / Growth Stages.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block before 50 DAT. No upper block: the source doesn't specify one, and for an indeterminate multi-harvest crop that keeps fruiting for months, a late pick isn't the same kind of problem as a late single-harvest grain crop -- same reasoning as tomato_r7.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Flag before 60 DAT. Sits above the 50-day hard-block floor: harvest logged between 50 and 60 days is physically accepted but flagged, since the stated typical window starts at ~60 DAT.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Harvesting logged more than 3 times in 7 days is blocked as anomalous data-padding. NEWLY IMPLEMENTED in the engine-fixes pass following the Medium-priority crop batch: this rule was previously flagged as entirely unimplementable, since the engine had no way to count occurrences of an operation within a rolling window -- it could only check a single date-offset from a dependency. Now uses max_occurrences/occurrence_window_days, added specifically to fix this rule (and rubber.json's analogous tapping/stimulation-frequency rules).
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Flag if harvest is logged more than 2 times in 7 days (i.e. '>2/week'), a softer threshold than the 3-times hard block above -- the source states both thresholds together as one escalating rule.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: ESTIMATE, flagged explicitly: the source ruleset's Stage 4 guidance for pepper is qualitative only ('pick ripe fruit; move quickly to market or dry chili types promptly'), with no stated hour/day figure -- unlike tomato's analogous rule, which the ruleset gives explicit 24-48 hour and 72 hour figures for. This rule borrows tomato's 0-2 day warning window as a reasonable proxy for 'quickly,' since both are perishable Solanaceae fruit crops, but this is an estimate carried over by analogy, not an independently stated figure for pepper. Flagged for agronomist/ruleset-author confirmation rather than presented as sourced.
validation_rules.source: Estimated by analogy to tomato_r_postharvest in tomato.json (itself sourced to the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset's tomato section) -- NOT independently stated for pepper in Section 13.

validation_rules.condition: Global rule: no operation may be logged with a date earlier than the previous operation's logged date for the same farm/cycle (no backdating that would reorder the sequence).
validation_rules.source: Inherited convention across this knowledge base.

validation_rules.condition: Land preparation must be logged at least 1 day before nursery establishment, and no more than 60 days before it.
validation_rules.internal_note: PLATFORM BUGFIX (second sweep): this dependency rule did not exist at all in the original file -- nursery_establishment could previously be logged with no land_preparation in its history whatsoever. Found via a systematic audit of every consecutive REQUIRED-to-REQUIRED workflow step pair across all 20 crops, run after the user asked whether the land-prep sequencing fix generalized to every stage. It did not, until this pass. min=1 day so same-day submissions are also caught, consistent with every other sequencing fix in this knowledge base.
validation_rules.source: N/A -- internal platform bugfix, not new agronomic sourcing. Max-day window (60 days) is a reasonable platform default matching similar transitions elsewhere in this file, not independently sourced from the Master Ruleset for this specific pair.

weather_preferences.notes: Not covered numerically in the source ruleset section for this crop -- carried over as a placeholder from general West African pepper agronomy references, same caveat as yam.json's and groundnut.json's weather_preferences. Flagged for agronomist review.

diseases.name: Pepper Veinal Mottle Virus (PVMV)
diseases.symptoms: Vein clearing, mottling, leaf distortion; aphid-transmitted, named directly in the source ruleset alongside mites and fruit fly as the crop's core IPM targets.
diseases.management: Vector (aphid) control, resistant varieties where available, scouting through vegetative and fruiting stages.
diseases.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 3 ('Manage Pepper Veinal Mottle Virus, mites and fruit fly through scouting and vector control').

diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt
diseases.symptoms: Sudden whole-plant wilting; shared with tomato per the source ruleset's own rotation-check rationale.
diseases.management: Avoid planting pepper immediately after tomato on the same plot -- the source ruleset names this explicitly as the reason for its (currently unimplementable) rotation-check rule. Crop rotation more broadly, resistant varieties.
diseases.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 1 ('Avoid planting immediately after tomato -- they share bacterial wilt and viruses').

pests.name: Mites
pests.symptoms: Leaf curling, bronzing, stippling from sap feeding.
pests.management: Scouting and vector control per the source ruleset's IPM guidance.
pests.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 3.

pests.name: Fruit Fly
pests.symptoms: Larvae develop inside ripening fruit, causing internal rot and premature drop.
pests.management: Scouting and vector control per the source ruleset's IPM guidance; prompt harvest of ripe fruit reduces the window of exposure.
pests.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Stage 3.

yield_model.expected_yield_per_hectare: 7.37 (Nigeria national average, FAO 2024 estimate); normal range 1.0 - 10.0
yield_model.unit: tonnes, cumulative across the whole 3-4 month harvest window
factors: split fertilizer adherence across the long fruiting window
yield_model.notes: Range taken directly from the source ruleset's Pass and first Warning tiers. Explicitly cumulative across the full multi-month picking season, not a single-event figure -- same framing the source ruleset uses for tomato. Earlier expected yield, kept as the record of what was replaced: 1.0 - 20.0.

tiers.message: Must be logged as a Disaster/Loss Event.
Severe disease (e.g., PVMV) or early field abandonment.
Optimized GAP management; flag for review.
Improbable open-field -- a single harvest likely logged as the total, or a unit typo.

yield_validation.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper), Yield Validation table. NOTE: the source table as written has an unaddressed gap between its stated '10.0-20.0 t/ha Soft Warning' tier and its '>35.0 t/ha Hard Block' tier, leaving 20.0-35.0 covered by neither -- same failure mode as yam.json and groundnut.json, which would make yield_validator.py raise an error on a plausible real value in that band. Resolved here by merging the source's two described warning bands ('10.0-20.0, Optimized GAP management' and the unaddressed 20.0-35.0 range) into a single greater_than 10.0 warning tier covering everything above Pass up to the Hard Block ceiling, rather than inventing a new numeric boundary the source doesn't state. Flagged for agronomist/ruleset-author confirmation.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - new crop, Medium-priority tier, built from Master Ruleset
version_history.summary: Initial file for Pepper (Rodo/Tatashe/Sombo), third of the 8 Medium-priority crops from the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset not yet in this knowledge base, built from Section 13. Structured closely on tomato.json's nursery/transplant/repeated-harvest pattern (day 0 = transplanting, harvest is can_repeat true with no once-only rule), since pepper shares tomato's Solanaceae vegetative curve per the source document's own framing. TWO rules named explicitly in the source document could NOT be implemented at all with this knowledge base's current engine, and are NOT approximated here -- flagged plainly rather than faked, per instruction to compile a full list of engine gaps for a dedicated review once all crops are done: (1) the rotation-check rule ('avoid planting immediately after tomato... system flags this from plot history') requires checking a DIFFERENT crop's history against this one -- engine.validator.validate_operation is deliberately scoped to a single crop_id's history per call (see its own docstring), so no rule in this schema can reference another crop's plot history at all, not even approximately. (2) The harvest-frequency rule ('harvesting logged more than 3 times in 7 days is blocked as anomalous data-padding, flag if >2/week') requires counting how many times an operation appears within a rolling day-window in history -- every existing validation_rule mechanic checks a single most-recent-dependency date-offset, not an occurrence count, so this rule type does not exist in the schema at all yet. Both are qualitatively different from this knowledge base's previously-flagged limitations (interior-band rules, duration-as-proxy modeling), which were all still expressible as some approximation -- these two are not expressible at all without new engine capability. Also resolved a yield_validation tier gap (20.0-35.0 t/ha) the same way as yam.json/groundnut.json, and flagged the post-harvest-handling timing rule as borrowed by analogy from tomato.json rather than independently sourced, since the source ruleset gives pepper only qualitative post-harvest guidance ('move quickly'), not a stated hour figure. Not yet agronomist-reviewed.
version_history.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 13 (Pepper).

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - engine-fixes pass, Group A
version_history.summary: Implemented the harvest-frequency rule (pepper_r_harvest_frequency_block/warn) that v1.0.0 flagged as entirely unimplementable, using the new max_occurrences/occurrence_window_days mechanism (added to schema.json/engine.validator in this same pass, specifically to fix this rule and rubber.json's analogous ones). Both thresholds from the source are now enforced: hard block at more than 3 harvest logs in 7 days, soft warning at more than 2. The rotation-check rule (avoid planting after tomato) remains unimplemented -- that is a Group C item (cross-crop plot history), out of scope for this engine-fixes pass, and still flagged on the land_preparation operation.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - platform bugfix, land-prep sequencing gate
version_history.summary: Bumped min_days_after_dependency from 0 to 1 on pepper_r1, in response to a real bug the user found while using the platform: land preparation could be logged and the very next dependent stage logged on the SAME DAY, with no gap enforced at all, even though the workflow conceptually expects one stage to be completed/settled before the next begins. min=0 technically meant '0 or more days later', which permitted same-day submissions. This is a data-authoring fix (a deliberate rule-value choice), not an engine bug -- the engine was correctly enforcing exactly what the rule said, the rule just said something too permissive. No maximum-day-window or severity changed, and no other rule in this file was touched.
version_history.source: N/A -- internal platform bugfix, not new agronomic sourcing.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - platform bugfix, land-prep sequencing gate
version_history.summary: Added pepper_r_land_prep_gate, a dependency rule that was MISSING ENTIRELY from this file, in response to a real bug the user found while using the platform: the affected operation(s) could previously be logged with no preceding dependency in history at all -- not same-day, not any particular window, just completely unenforced. Confirmed via a test submission with empty history before this fix (the operation passed clean with zero warnings). Now requires at least 1 day after the dependency, closing the gap. This is a data-authoring fix (a rule that should have existed but didn't), not an engine bug.

version_history.summary: Added pepper_r_seq_land_preparation_nursery_establishment. Found via a systematic audit of every consecutive REQUIRED-to-REQUIRED workflow step pair across all 20 crops, run after the user asked whether the land-prep sequencing fix (first sweep) generalized to every stage transition. It did not -- this file had one or more later-stage transitions where the next required step could be logged with no record of the preceding required step ever existing, the same bug class as the original land-prep gap. min=1 day so same-day submissions are also caught. Confirmed via scenario testing that the affected operation(s) now correctly require their dependency to exist first.

version_history.summary: Added harvest_estimate: typical yield 7.37 t/ha (FAO national average, 2024, an FAO estimate), normal range 1.0 to 10.0 t/ha (ruleset low, best case capped at twice the typical) and its sources.

harvest_estimate.yield_basis: fresh green fruit, added up over the whole harvest period
harvest_estimate.method: Typical is the FAO national average for Nigeria in 2024. The low end is the crop's normal low from the yield checks (the CEO's ruleset). The high end is that ruleset's best case, capped at twice the typical yield, so it stays close to what farms really get (CEO decision, 25 Oct 2026). The harvest window is the expected window in the crop's timing rules, where they give one. The range is what is normal for a farm, not a forecast for this one.
caveats: National averages hide the spread between farms, so a single farm can be well outside the typical figure.
FAO flags the 2024 figure for this crop as its own estimate (flag E), not a figure reported by Nigeria. It is weaker evidence than the figures for maize or soybean.
Not a prediction for this farm: it does not know this season's rain, soil, seed or care.
The high end is capped at twice the typical yield (10.0 t/ha). The ruleset's own best case is 10.0 t/ha, which a well-run farm can reach but few farms do.
FAO's pepper figure barely changes (7.4 to 7.6 t/ha for ten years), which suggests it is a modelled value rather than a survey result.
The yield is the total picked over the whole harvest period, not one picking.

harvest_estimate.timing_note: The crop rules give the earliest sensible harvest (60 days after transplanting) but no latest date, because peppers are picked over several months, so no harvest window is shown.
